1. What conclusion can you reach about the responses to this question?
- I can conclude that each student uses their 5 minutes before class to their best ability on what works for them
- Each student shares similar or unique things that help them be ready before class
2. Is the default summary or visualization helpful? How could it be improved?
- Yes, it is helpful because it gives a clear view of the data of when these submissions were submitted as well as the time it was submitted
- I don't see anything for this to be needing to be improved
3. For questions with an “Other” option, where can you find the actual text of those responses? Do you notice anything that might be tricky about analyzing these?
- You can find those responses along with all the Yes/No responses
- For me I don't see this being tricky at all
4. For questions calling for a written response, what challenges do you notice about finding trends or patterns in the answers provided?
- Some responses are longer than the cell on the file, so it makes it tough to read some of them
5. Now that you can see the responses, how might you recommend rephrasing this or question or the response options in a future survey?
- I would recommend rephrasing some of the responses where there not too long, where it can be short and simple
6. Is there anything that surprised you about the survey responses?
- I was surprised on how many students said that they make sure their devices are charged and working properly before class starts
7. Looking at the responses to questions 1 and 5, are there any ideas you might try to include in your morning routine, or any questions that you are also curious about?
- For my routine I would like to try to ensure that my devices are working correctly before I go get my coffee ready, that way there's no malfunction while I'm in class
8. Pretend you are the instructor. Is there anything you can learn from this survey to help in how you approach teaching this class?

- The approach I would bring to this class is to try and have office hours after class for some students who still might be unsure on the material or needs any clarification about the work needed to be done
9. Again, pretend you are the instructor. Do you think it was helpful or not helpful to make this survey anonymous? Why or why not? (If you can see both pros and cons, you may include both.)

- I see it as a pro to make this survey anonymous because it gives students confidence and security to address their situation or their struggles, that way me as an instructor can understand overall on what to do to help the class
